official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2021 serious-water-stress classification was made for water-company areas and is not a parcel-scale planning designation.
Current Approved Document G retains the mandatory new-dwelling water-efficiency framework, including 125 litres/person/day and the optional 110 litres/person/day route where applicable.
A local planning authority can require the optional standard only where the planning-policy and evidence requirements are satisfied; serious water stress alone is not a parcel permission outcome.

The 2025 consultation proposed tighter future standards of 105 and 100 litres/person/day; a consultation proposal must not be treated as current operative Building Regulations on 26 July 2026 without enacted change.

The June 2026 water resources planning guideline uses a long-term company planning ambition of no greater than 110 litres/person/day by 2050, which is distinct from a building-control compliance threshold for an individual dwelling.
Water-stress classification concerns resource planning and metering context and does not prove a specific development has a water connection or sufficient network capacity.
Planning policy, Building Regulations and water-company resource planning operate through distinct decision and compliance routes.
Water-stress or efficiency status does not establish ownership, connection capacity, planning permission or final development yield.

core_rules: water-stress area is not parcel planning designation
planning optional standard needs policy evidence
2025 consultation proposal is not current enacted standard
2050 PCC ambition is not parcel compliance threshold
water stress is not connection capacity proof
Building Regulations and planning remain distinct
water-company plan is not planning permission
efficiency target does not calculate development yield
future standard must retain commencement status
connection and requisition evidence remains separate
no parcel water-stress clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Environment Agency, Defra, MHCLG, GOV.UK and legislation sources checked 2026-07-26. 2021 classification, current Approved Document G, 2025 consultation and June 2026 WRMP guidance kept temporally distinct; no parcel promotion.
